blocks.body:
## Decision

Adopt the process-local WGPU software graph as an explicit low-latency `CapturedCodecDecode` policy, not as the default codec path. The packed arena lowers all five paired device estimates and nearly eliminates host graph-construction time. Its median observed NVML cost is now 131 MiB rather than the original 172 MiB, but the ordinary decode path remains the memory-saving default.

## Packed reuse improves latency without the original arena overhead

The session reuses compiled pipelines, bind groups, immediate values, resource transitions, and dispatch order. Non-overlapping intermediates now share aligned 64 MiB sliced pages, with an exclusive fallback for larger allocations. Per request it performs one bit-preserving GPU-to-GPU latent copy, replays the fixed codec graph, and reads back only final audio. Across five fresh processes, the median paired-block improvement was 0.349 ms at device completion and 0.288 ms through CPU readback. Median host enqueue fell from 0.522 ms to 0.0025 ms.

## Arena packing removes about 40 MiB without giving back speed

The dedicated graph arena reserves 134,217,728 additional allocator bytes while retaining only 192,000 additional logical in-use bytes for final audio. That is 42,284,544 bytes less reservation than the original exclusive-page arena. Median NVML peak was 1,317 MiB with the graph session and 1,186 MiB in independent normal-only processes, a 41 MiB reduction from the earlier graph campaign's median peak. The comparison to the earlier campaign is descriptive only; no old timing sample is pooled into the new estimator.

## Runtime and API contract

`CapturedCodecDecode<'model>` borrows the codec so captured weights cannot be dropped, owns stable input/output buffers, and requires `&mut self` to serialize update and replay. Its safe method returns owned F32 CPU audio; reusable GPU output tensors never escape. Capture rejects synchronization, readback, host writes, profiling, memory-policy mutation, graph nesting, unknown graphs, and cross-stream replay. Dynamic indirect dispatch buffers are retained. Graph destruction synchronizes before releasing its arena.

## Correctness and validation

All graph and normal outputs were bitwise equal with waveform SHA-256 `113ba560546d82a3112332ac67b3cea5d5b83b407109d3df3817e5b82b609e05`; all five paired sessions reported zero uncaptured WGPU errors. Against the independently pinned F16 fixture: max absolute error 0.00341797, RMSE 0.000213971, SNR 56.0742 dB, cosine 0.999998775. The arena changes allocation only; captured operation order, bindings, and numeric kernels are unchanged.

## Portability, limitations, and next work

The implementation uses shared WGPU allocation APIs and rounds page sizes to the adapter's required alignment; it is intended for Vulkan, Metal, DX12, and native WebGPU. Only NVIDIA/Vulkan is measured here, so portability remains a source-level claim. Pipelines and graphs are process-local and are not serialized across launches. Each graph is fixed-shape, and one graph arena per simultaneously resident shape would multiply the 128 MiB reservation. Next steps are capture of the final F32 consumer transform, a bounded shape-session policy, and Metal/DX12 compile-and-accuracy smoke tests.

## Reproduction

Use source commit `4d8b573453e1530d8009847c1b5b71c71ec3f627`, binary SHA-256 `6b0a6a3f93376a20c255f5217a3b055707e272972ee8a765b63f04afcb0e02ce`, fixture SHA-256 `08663e52df6c63eea7ebf5ae2ba35778bdb5bc7d20cd06e430e855a86174229e`, and codec SHA-256 `b14a25da5d68bf779d8c44a40706ddc7c4819cb60489b2a80a6408ca03c514fb`. Run five fresh paired sessions with five warmups and ten ABBA/BAAB blocks; sample NVML every 100 ms. Run five separate normal-only fresh processes for VRAM control. The fresh campaign `SHA256SUMS` digest is `18ce0e0e7619a8c817075d992114d4f19cfeac2c634387f0bd57b2b3d02eda44`; verify it before aggregation.
